Commentary.Commentary: Right then, that’s all from us for this rain-affected encounter. Both the captains pose with the trophy as the T20I series gets shared honors. England will now head to Ireland for a three-match T20I series, while South Africa's next international challenge is an all-format tour of Pakistan next month. Switch your tabs to follow all the action from the Asia Cup 2025 contest between India and Pakistan, which is setting up nicely in Dubai. Until then, cheers and goodbye!

England captain Harry Brook praised their recent game, saying it was a shame the weather ruined it. He highlighted the dominating performance against a strong South African side, which will boost their confidence moving forward. Brook expressed his faith in his teammate, believing he will continue to perform well alongside Jos Buttler. He also mentioned the team's potential to score 300 or more again, given their strong lineup. Looking ahead, Brook mentioned the upcoming series against New Zealand and the Ashes, and seemed to be looking forward to some time off before those matches.

South Africa captain Aiden Markram reflected on the team's recent performances, acknowledging that the second game didn't go their way after a quick win in the first match. He highlighted the importance of adaptability in planning, noting that sometimes teams need to tap into unexpected skills to succeed. Markram expressed optimism about the lessons learned from the tour against Australia, emphasizing that the T20 squad is working towards the World Cup and aims to continue improving.

Phil Salt, the Player of the Series, expressed a sense of frustration due to the weather. He mentioned that the plan on Friday was to keep the opposition under pressure. Salt enjoyed opening with Jos, citing their long-standing partnership and familiarity with each other's game. Looking ahead, he noted that Ireland would be a challenging opponent, acknowledging their good recent form and the team's upcoming task. Salt seemed to relish the opportunity, describing Ireland as "always a good place to be."
Presentation time...

Persistent rain has had the final say, with the match abandoned without a ball being bowled, not even the toss could take place. Given the bleak weather forecast in Nottingham, this outcome was always on the cards. It’s a disappointing end to what had been shaping up as a thrilling T20I series, locked at 1-1 coming into the decider. South Africa edged a rain-affected clash in Cardiff, while England bounced back in style with a dominant batting display in Manchester. With the momentum evenly poised, today’s finale promised fireworks, but instead, we’re left with a damp squib. The series ends all square, with fans and players alike left wondering what might have been a fitting finale of the England summer.

UPDATE - 3.12 pm GMT - The rain has intensified, making this the heaviest spell we've seen so far today. The prospects of play are looking increasingly uncertain, though we're still some time away from the official cut-off. Fingers crossed for a break in the weather and at least a shortened contest.
UPDATE - 2.38 pm GMT - There's no new update to share. Heavy rain is continuing to fall at Trent Bridge, resulting in still conditions, and the match has started losing overs.

Other news from the cricketing world -  In the Asia Cup 2025 clash, Pakistan has won the toss and elected to bat first against India. Both teams have opted to field an unchanged XI from their previous matches. Meanwhile, in the women's bilateral ODI series between India and Australia, India set a competitive target of 281 runs. In response, Australia is well-placed at 171/2 after 28 overs, needing 111 more runs from 22 overs with 8 wickets in hand.

UPDATE - 1.59 pm GMT - The rain continues to fall, and the covers remain firmly in place. Overs will start being lost from 3:30 PM local time. There's no word yet on the cut-off time for a potential five-over showdown. Stay tuned for further updates.
UPDATE - 1.15 GMT - Oh No! Just as the captains were in the middle for the toss, the rain has gotten heavier, and the covers are back on. The toss is delayed again.
UPDATE - 1.13 GMT - Good news, everyone! The rain has cleared, and the toss is coming up shortly. Fingers crossed for a full match ahead!

England's Saqib Mahmood has been ruled out of both this match and next week's T20I series against Ireland due to a knee injury that will require surgery. Scott Currie has been called up as his replacement in the England squad.

UPDATE -  1.04 pm GMT - It's currently raining at Trent Bridge and the covers are on. Skies are grey and things look gloomy, but let's hope the weather gets better and we can get some action. The Toss is delayed.

One thing that could throw a curveball into proceedings is the weather. Showers are in the forecast and could interrupt the action, but let’s hope the rain stays away and we get a full, thrilling finale. So, who are you backing in the series decider? Toss and team news coming up shortly. Stay tuned!

As for South Africa, they’ll be eager to bounce back after a morale-crushing defeat. Their bowlers were taken to the cleaners, conceding over 300 runs for the first time in a T20I. Kwena Maphaka and Bjorn Fortuin offered brief moments of control, but the damage was done early. Chasing 305, the Proteas got off to a decent start through Aiden Markram and Ryan Rickelton, but the innings unravelled quickly thereafter. They were eventually bundled out for 158, falling well short. Today presents a fresh opportunity, and South Africa will be desperate to reset, respond, and clinch the series, but it won’t be easy against a confident and well-rounded English side.

After a disappointing start in the opening match, England roared back in the second T20I with a record-breaking 146-run win. The hosts posted a towering 304/2 after being asked to bat first as Jos Buttler led the charge with a brutal 83 off just 30 balls, while Phil Salt lit up the evening with an unbeaten 141 off 60 balls, a career-best knock. Explosive cameos from Jacob Bethell and Harry Brook helped England cross the 300-mark in style. With the ball, England’s bowlers were clinical. Jofra Archer, Sam Curran, Liam Dawson, and Will Jacks shared the wickets as South Africa were bowled out for 158 inside 17 overs, sealing a dominant win and squaring the series. Now, with all to play for, England will be aiming to carry that momentum into today’s game, especially with batting-friendly conditions expected at Trent Bridge.

Hello and welcome to our coverage of the third and final T20I between England and South Africa from Trent Bridge in Nottingham. With the series level at 1-1, today’s decider promises to be a high-octane clash, with both sides set to leave it all on the field in pursuit of the series trophy.
…MATCHDAY…

One could not have asked for a more entertaining white-ball series than the England-South Africa one. The ODI series belonged to the Proteas with the scoreline of 2-1, but the hosts, England, ensured they left their mark on the last ODI and entered the T20I series with great confidence and momentum. The weather significantly influenced the first T20I, and the visitors were good enough to defeat the English side and take the lead in the three-match T20I series. But the hosts were raring to make a comeback in the second match, and they grandly did that. Batting first, they breached the 300-run mark and then bundled out South Africa for 158 runs to level the series 1-1. Now, we have reached the last match of the tour, and it will be the decider of the T20I series at Trent Bridge in Nottingham. England have looked like a dominant force in the T20Is, and they would fancy their chances of winning this decider to bag the series in their favour. Their batting looks lethal, with Phil Salt smashing a record-breaking unbeaten 141 in the last game, and alongside him is the veteran Jos Buttler, who is in top-notch form. In the middle, Harry Brook and Jacob Bethell have firm control of the batting line-up, and in the lower-middle order, they have the brute power of Will Jacks, Tom Banton, and Sam Curran. Similarly, Jofra Archer is breathing fire in the bowling alley, alongside the left-arm seamer Luke Wood. Liam Dawson and Adil Rashid have perfectly complemented them in the spin bowling department. So as a whole, the English side looks like a complete unit and would be backing themselves to win this contest. South Africa started the T20I series well with a win, but the defeat in the last encounter must have taken them aback, and they would look to regroup, rethink, and reanalyse their game plans to showcase a better performance in the decider. Their top order batting looks stagnant, with Ryan Rickelton and Lhuan-dre Pretorius failing to get themselves going the way the team would have wanted. And the inconsistency of Dewald Brevis in the middle order is making their batting order a bit more vulnerable. Donovan Ferreira has looked promising until now and would look to build on his performances. The injury woes for the Proteas have continued in the T20I series and they are without the services of Keshav Maharaj due to his groin injury. As a result, their spin bowling department doesn't seem to be threatening at all. So in the bowling assault, their hopes lie in the shoulders of Kagiso Rabada and Marco Jansen to get them some early breakthroughs and give them an early advantage in the game. It promises to be a thrilling decider between the two sides, and the hosts do hold a psychological advantage ahead of this game. Still, the Proteas cannot be written off given their domination in the entire tour, and they would be backing themselves to start afresh and look to seal the T20I series as well. So, it will be interesting to see which team comes out on top and gets the desired result in their favour.
